claude.sample_unit: TDA brochures (each with AI-generated counterparts across four conditions)

links.outcome: Readability of professional society patient brochures versus recommended reading level
links.effect: TDA brochures mean Ateşman score 59.08 ± 5.80, 'medium difficulty', ranging from 48.0 (difficult) to 70.3; potential barrier given 64.6% inadequate/problematic health literacy.
links.quote: The mean readability score for the original brochures was 59.08 ± 5.80, placing the material in the “medium difficulty” category according to the Ateşman Index classification.

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education text versus original brochures, default and low-literacy prompted
links.effect: All AI groups scored higher than TDA (59.08): ChatGPT 62.66, prompted ChatGPT 68.31, Gemini 66.63, prompted Gemini 68.98 (all p<0.05; r 0.242-0.753). No expert review of accuracy.
links.quote: Pairwise comparisons confirmed that all AI-generated texts, regardless of the specific model or prompting strategy employed, scored significantly higher than the standard TDA brochures: TDA versus ChatGPT (p = 0.047; r = 0.242), TDA versus prompted ChatGPT (p < 0.001; r = 0.667), TDA versus Gemini (p < 0.001; r = 0.548), and TDA versus prompted Gemini (p < 0.001; r = 0.753).

unlisted_practices: Low-literacy (sixth-grade) prompting of LLMs to improve readability of patient education materials
Hybrid approach using AI to simplify society-authored patient education content

openai.sample_unit: TDA patient education brochures with AI-generated counterparts

links.effect: Default Gemini readability 66.63 versus ChatGPT 62.66; p=0.004; r=0.306.
links.quote: Gemini produced significantly more readable texts than ChatGPT in the absence of specific prompts (66.63 versus 62.66; p = 0.004; r = 0.306).

links.outcome: readability of AI-generated patient education materials
links.effect: Means: TDA 59.08; ChatGPT 62.66; prompted ChatGPT 68.31; Gemini 66.63; prompted Gemini 68.98; all AI versus TDA p=0.047 to p<0.001.
links.quote: Pairwise comparisons confirmed that all AI-generated texts, regardless of the specific model or prompting strategy employed, scored significantly higher than the standard TDA brochures: TDA versus ChatGPT (p = 0.047; r = 0.242), TDA versus prompted ChatGPT (p < 0.001; r = 0.667), TDA versus Gemini (p < 0.001; r = 0.548), and TDA versus prompted Gemini (p < 0.001; r = 0.753).

links.outcome: effect of low-literacy prompt on readability
links.effect: Specific prompting improved ChatGPT (p<0.001), but Gemini scores did not significantly change.
links.quote: While specific prompting significantly improved ChatGPT performance (p < 0.001), no significant change was observed in Gemini scores, which were already high in the default condition.

links.outcome: Ateşman readability score of AI-generated patient education materials
links.effect: Prompting improved ChatGPT readability from 62.66 to 68.31 (p < 0.001, r = 0.425), but did not significantly improve Gemini (66.63 vs 68.98, p = 0.169); both exceeded TDA brochures (59.08, p < 0.05).
links.quote: While specific prompting significantly improved ChatGPT performance (p < 0.001), no significant change was observed in Gemini scores, which were already high in the default condition.
